drafted_from: tool:extract-sound's own row in tools/media-composition/tool-rows.json (its argv is one ffmpeg command: no script, mono, 16 kHz, 64 kb/s), and that command run on a synthetic 7 second clip
start_here: Say to your AI: "Take the sound out of my video as a small audio file so I can transcribe it." It runs tool:extract-sound and saves an MP3 in your files.
no_lists_because: It reads one video you name and saves its sound as one file, so it keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Find your video's identity in your files: 1f: then 64 hex.
2. Say "Extract the sound from this video"; the tool takes only the video.

3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:extract-sound. It answers {"files": {"sound": {identity, bytes, media_type, name}}}, or {"error": "what to change"}.
4. Give files.sound.identity to the speech-to-text tool, or keep the MP3: it is mono 16 kHz at 64 kb/s, about 0.5 MB a minute.

worked_examples.title: A 7 second clip becomes a 57 KB MP3
worked_examples.ask: Take the sound out of my video.
worked_examples.given: read from the tool row's argv (ffmpeg -vn -ac 1 -ar 16000 -b:a 64k) and run on a 7 second clip: 7 s at 64 kb/s is about 56 KB
